Replaced with the accurate model: personal IDs are not typeable by prefix; corporate/registered entities occupy the 5XX-million block.

Expert MAJOR (all-zeros trap) fixed: validate_israeli_id('000000000') and validate_israeli_id('') both returned True (empty zero-pads into all-zeros, which passes Luhn). Added an explicit reject plus a gotcha. This is the most common sentinel/empty-field false positive in production KYC.

lessons: CRITICAL FIX (code): validate_israeli_id gated on str.isdigit(), which is True for Arabic-Indic digits and superscripts. Verified before the fix: '12345678²' raised ValueError (a 500 in production) and '١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٢' returned True, silently accepting a string the DB and the registry lookup treat as a different value. Now normalized through re.sub(r'[^0-9]','',s).zfill(9) and gated with re.fullmatch(r'[0-9]{9}'). The inline snippet in both SKILL files was updated to match, since that is the code readers actually copy.

CRITICAL FIX (compliance): the privacy gotcha said 'hash or tokenize before persisting'. Unkeyed hashing of a 9-digit ID is not protection: the keyspace is under 10^9 and the check digit cuts it further, so a hashed column is exhaustively reversible. Now requires HMAC-SHA256 with a pepper held outside the DB, or a tokenization vault.

CRITICAL FIX (compliance): the DPO scope was stated as a bare headcount ('reaches entities processing data on more than 10,000 people'). That is wrong compliance advice. The Authority's final opinion attaches the duty to public bodies and their holders, to bodies TRADING in data whose database covers more than 10,000 people, to bodies engaged in ongoing systematic monitoring, and to controllers/holders whose main business is large-scale processing of specially sensitive data. Body now states the qualifying conditions verbatim-grounded, and the evidence raw_snippet was extended to cover them (it previously quoted only the publication sentence, so the 10,000 figure was ungrounded).

MAJOR FIX (code): generate_test_id could emit '000000000', which the validator rejects as a sentinel, and a prefix longer than 8 produced an 11-character string (verified: generate_test_id('1234567890') -> '12345678903'). Prefix is now validated as \\d{0,8} and the all-zero draw is re-rolled.

MAJOR FIX (content): added the single most consequential omission for Israeli business software: a self-employed person's mispar osek (murshe or patur) IS their personal 9-digit Teudat Zehut, not a 5x registered-entity number. A 'business number' field that accepts only 5x rejects every osek patur in the country.

PROCESS, the recurring defect again but in a new shape: repointing the Amendment 13 citation from the paywalled IAPP article to law.co.il updated the URL in both SKILL files and evidence.json but left the LINK LABEL reading '(IAPP analysis)' / '(ניתוח IAPP)', so the body misattributed the publisher. Old-value propagation is not only about figures: when a citation moves, the label, the anchor text and the surrounding prose all carry the old value too.

EVIDENCE TOOLING: three snippets failed --check-sources purely because the quoted phrase is split across HTML tags on the source page, so the raw-HTML substring matcher cannot see it contiguously. Two were re-anchored to the longest contiguous genuine fragment; the sanction figure was marked verified_via=browser after reading the rendered text directly. CARRY: test-data ethics are one sentence. The TZ space is densely allocated, so a randomly generated 'test' ID is very likely a living person's real ID and must never reach seed data, staging emails, screenshots or demo tenants.

CARRY: the 2017 information-security regulations (database tiering basic/medium/high, access logging, segregation, annual review) are what actually govern a database of ID numbers and are absent, as is the narrowed database-registration duty and the extraterritorial reach to non-Israeli processors.

CARRY: no golden test-vector table in references/id-formats.md (known-valid, transposition, off-by-one check digit, all-zeros, 8-digit-with-dropped-zero), and no note that a TZ is not a safe immutable primary key.

The prose was right and the code was wrong, which is why nothing caught this for two cycles. Reading SKILL.md tells you the all-zeros sentinel is a trap; only RUNNING the script showed the script falls into it.

The defect was in input handling, not in the algorithm. A deterministic algorithm invites the assumption that a deterministic script is fine. Test the BOUNDARY of the input domain, not the middle: empty, whitespace, letters, punctuation, over-length, and a decimal point.

Stripping every non-digit with a regex is the natural-looking one-liner and it is the bug. It deletes offending characters instead of reporting them, so the validator accepts garbage silently. The skill recommended it in Troubleshooting, so the bad pattern was being taught, not just used.

A single boolean return cannot express three outcomes. Separating malformed input from a failed check digit needed an exit-code contract (0 valid, 1 bad check digit, 2 malformed), and the library already held the information the CLI was discarding.
Cross-checking against an independently written implementation of the same published algorithm is cheap, and is what allowed the arithmetic to be declared sound by evidence rather than by inspection.

A fix can reach the CLI and miss the library under it. 1.3.0 removed the strip-every-non-digit regex from the CLI path while normalize_id() kept it as a fallback, so validate_israeli_id('62819482.1') still returned True. Test the importable functions, not just the command line.

The inline code in SKILL.md is what readers copy, and it drifts from the script. Exec every fenced Python/JS block against the golden vectors each cycle (this cycle: generator guard missing inline, then input handling).

The check-digit weights 1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1 are a palindrome, so a reversed 9-digit ID always passes. The skill had listed RTL reversal as a cause of check FAILURE for several cycles; caught only by an expert who ran 20,000 reversals.

Accepting more input is a security decision. Discarding 'invisible' characters to fix paste false negatives briefly let bidi overrides through ('\u202e287654321' displays as 123456782). Only BN-class zero-width characters may be dropped inside a number; LRM/RLM/ALM and line breaks only at the ends; overrides and isolates never.
